scope: LIVE on the camera, firmware 5.02.0.V91, model w71c1. Host-pulsed MOVON/MOVOFF, FHD CinemaDNG, hook at 0xC0722AFC. Everything the engine touched is inside our own retained 4 MiB block; seg was never read for its buffer nor written, and every frame reached the card as stock.
headline: the hardware lossless-JPEG codec was driven ASYNCHRONOUSLY by our own code, from inside the CinemaDNG writer hook, during a live recording: submit and return on one frame, completion observed on the next. The destination holds a real lossless JPEG.

1_the_owner_word_is_not_a_busy_flag.was_believed: 1 = busy; our own preflight gated on == 0 and refused three live runs in a row with ERR_MODE_BUSY (8). That refusal was reported to the operator as 'the camera is stuck'. The operator said it was not stuck. The operator was right.
1_the_owner_word_is_not_a_busy_flag.is: an owner selector. 0 = closed, 1 and 2 = open and held by that client. C062FFF8 latches 1 and installs the callback at +0x04 from request+0x2C; the mode-2 setup latches 2 and installs at +0x38. The mode-1 starter C0630208 and the mode-2 starter C06303F8 each gate on their own value.
1_the_owner_word_is_not_a_busy_flag.fix: both preflights and both host predicates now refuse only a value no setup path can produce (cmp #2 / bhi, and <= 2 on the host). Live: power_preflight PASS and scratch_preflight PASS with codec_mode = 1.
1_the_owner_word_is_not_a_busy_flag.evidence: [C] capstone; [L] three refusals then two passes

2_programming_the_engine_is_not_starting.is: C062FFF8 validates the request, memcpys 0x30 bytes to 0xC37CF884, writes every engine register at 0x300D0040, installs the callback and latches mode 1 - and stops. The GO bit is [0x300D0000] |= 2, set ONLY by the mode-1 starter C0630208 (thumb wrapper C062FEB1).
2_programming_the_engine_is_not_starting.fix: PHASE 11 now calls C062FEB1 immediately after the submit and records its return. Live: start_ret = 0.

3_the_completion_path_needs_the_device_O.was_believed: nothing; this step had simply never been looked for.
3_the_completion_path_needs_the_device_O.is: completion is hardware -> IRQ 0x29 -> C0630431 -> [0xC37CF880] -> set_flg. The IRQ handler is installed and enabled only by the open routine C062FEE8, which latches 'installed' in 0xC37CF878. That word read 0x00000000 live: the ISR had NEVER been installed this boot, so the hardware could finish and nothing could signal it.
the_close_C062FF68: [0xC37CF87C] = 0   <-- this is what writes the owner word back to 0
returns 0 on success. The ISR install latch 0xC37CF878 stays 1; only the enable is toggled.
3_the_completion_path_needs_the_device_O.why_the_synchronous_path_never_hit_this: F_ENC's own chain contains the open. Bypassing F_ENC to go asynchronous bypassed the open with it.
3_the_completion_path_needs_the_device_O.evidence: [L] 0xC37CF878 = 0 before, = 1 after; [C] capstone for both routines

the_result.how_it_was_driven: preflight (clip) -> scratch (clip) -> arm async-submit -> HOST callfn C062FEE9 (open) -> clip -> read -> HOST callfn C062FF69 (close) -> release
the_result.reading_the_returns: F_INIT and F_SIZE return 1 on SUCCESS - F_INIT's tail is cmp r0,#0 / moveq r1,#1 / movne r1,#0, so the inner 0 becomes 1. init_ret = 1 was never an error.
the_result.the_pattern: 1 = bit 0 = done. Bit 2 = error is NOT set. On the three failed runs it was 0x442, which contains neither bit - twai_flg does not write the pattern on E_TMOUT.
the_result.timing: 26,073 microseconds from submit to the poll that OBSERVED completion, so the true encode time is <= 26.1 ms. One FHD frame's compression fits inside one 41.7 ms frame period, and asynchronously it overlaps.

the_output_is_a_real_lossless_jpeg.decoded: SOI, then SOF3 (lossless JPEG) length 0x000E, precision 0x0C = 12 bits, 0x0170 = 368 rows, 0x0200 = 512 columns, 1 component, sampling 0x11, Tq 0; then two DHT segments. 512x368 is exactly the tile geometry the probe declared.

the_size_table.decoded: big-endian: 0x5C51 = 23,633 bytes for five tiles and 0x5C58 = 23,640 for the sixth, total about 141,810 bytes
the_size_table.ratio: 141,810 of 3,165,360 source bytes = 4.5 percent, on the deliberately compressible synthetic source (samples alternating 1024 and 3072)

the_result.the_clip: recorded normally. The stop pulse needed a second attempt (is_recording read 1 twice), which is the documented MOVON behaviour, not a fault of the probe.

second_run_with_the_size_table_corrected.why: the first run completed a real encode and still reported sum 0. F_SIZE delegates to C062FA48, which takes the table pointer from [0xC302CDD4+0x10] and the LOOP BOUND from [0xC302CDEC], then byte-reverses each entry into the caller's array. The probe had pointed the hardware at table + round_up(len, 1024) - 0x400 past where F_SIZE looks - and the tile count is set by the driver C062F6F8, which this phase deliberately does not run, so the loop ran zero times.
the_fix: request+0x24 now carries the engine's own table pointer (A_ENG10) verbatim
the phase publishes PROBE_TILES to 0xC302CDEC before submitting. Safe during recording because the camera writes RAW and compresses nothing, so the codec has no other user.
net zero bytes: the round-up arithmetic that was removed paid for the tile-count store, and async-submit is still exactly 1792
second_run_with_the_size_table_corrected.the_sum_is_now_right: 141,805 bytes, and it agrees EXACTLY with the table read by hand: 5 tiles at 0x5C51 = 23,633 plus one at 0x5C58 = 23,640. 141,805 of 3,165,360 source bytes = 4.48 percent.
second_run_with_the_size_table_corrected.table_now_where_F_SIZE_reads: 0x45568000: 515C0000 x5 then 585C0000, big-endian entries as the hardware writes them
second_run_with_the_size_table_corrected.destination: FF D8 FF C3 again, unchanged
second_run_with_the_size_table_corrected.guards: all four 0xA55AA55A; codec closed with C062FF69 and the block released, free_result 0
second_run_with_the_size_table_corrected.why_this_matters_beyond_tidiness: the DNG's tile offset table needs the per-tile byte counts. Getting them out through the firmware's own F_SIZE, rather than by a host read, is a requirement of the architecture and not a reporting nicety.

the_request_abi_now_fully_read.note: C0630178..C0630202 is the SECOND HALF of C062FFF8 - the push at C062FFFC and the pop at C0630202 match. Everything below is one function.
the_request_abi_now_fully_read.+0x08: depth code: 0 -> 12 bits, 1 -> 14, 2 -> 16, 3 -> 10; anything else is refused
the_request_abi_now_fully_read.+0x18: SOURCE LENGTH, 1 KiB aligned (it is ADDED to +0x14 at C0630198 to program 0x300D008C)
the_request_abi_now_fully_read.+0x20: DESTINATION LENGTH, 1 KiB aligned (added to +0x1C at C06301B8)
the_request_abi_now_fully_read.+0x2C: COMPLETION CALLBACK, not validated; C06301EC installs it at [0xC37CF880]
the_request_abi_now_fully_read.all_five_1KiB_checks: C06300A6..C06300C2, lsls #0x16 on each; any failure returns 1 without touching the hardware

corrections.what_was_wrong: 'nothing in the image ever writes 0 back to 0xC37CF87C', stated earlier today and written into the source comment and the test docstring.
corrections.why_it_was_wrong: the literal scan required the movw/movt pair to be adjacent. At C062FF70 a movs sits between them, so the close routine's write was missed.
corrections.the_truth: C062FF7A writes 0. The word means closed (0) versus open and owned (1 or 2). The gate relaxation to 'refuse only what no setup path can latch' remains correct; only the stated reason was wrong.

corrections.what_was_wrong: ERR_MODE_BUSY on three consecutive runs was attributed to 'the self-issued submit left the codec marked busy and nothing clears it', and the operator was told a power cycle was required.
corrections.the_truth: the refusal was our own gate misreading a normal owner value. No power cycle was needed and the camera was never stuck.

corrections.what_was_wrong: '+0x04 of the engine block is the source length, and it read 0, so we submitted a zero-length job' - said in the same breath as reading the record.
corrections.the_truth: that word is in the ENGINE PARAMETER BLOCK 0xC302CDD4, which the probe never uses; it reads ENG0/8/C/10/14. The request was well formed and submit_ret = 0 was genuine.

corrections.what_was_wrong: 'request+0x18 was given PROBE_DECLARED (0x305000) where it should be the SOURCE length (0x304CB0)', written into this ledger's first draft.
corrections.the_truth: +0x18 must be 1 KiB aligned - C06300AC checks it - and PROBE_DECLARED is defined as round_up(12*1936*1090/8, 1024), which IS the rounded source length. The field was correct; the objection was not. The constant's name is what misled, not the value.

corrections.what_was_wrong: 'the recorded sum is 0 because the probe sums the table at TABLE_OFF while the request points the engine at TABLE_OFF + 0x400'.
corrections.the_truth: half right. The probe never sums a table: it calls F_SIZE. The two real causes were the misplaced table pointer AND the unset tile count at 0xC302CDEC. Both are fixed and the second run reports sum 141805.

known_imperfections_in_the_probe_not_in_: none outstanding. Both items recorded earlier today are resolved or were wrong; see corrections.
what_this_unblocks: the dynamic architecture's executable path. Hijack a frame, submit its compression, return immediately, let later frames pass, observe completion on a later writer call, then hand the compressed payload to CinemaDNG as a late submit. Every step of that is now measured rather than assumed. The remaining open question is unchanged and is NOT about the codec: every writer call must still produce a file, because skipping one aborts the clip.
operator_authorisations_used: calling C062FEE9 (open) and C062FF69 (close) from the host, agreed to explicitly after the risk was stated: no paired close inside the open, so power and clock stay on until closed; reversible by a power cycle
